title: 2009 HMMT November Guts Problem 29
statement: For how many integer values of \(b\) does there exist a polynomial function with integer coefficients such that \(f(2)=2010\) and \(f(b)=8\) ?

solutions.text: 32 We can take \(f(x)=-\frac{2002}{d}(x-b)+2010\) for all divisors \(d\) of -2002 . To see that we can't get any others, note that \(b-2\) must divide \(f(b)-f(2)\), so \(b-2\) divides -2002 (this is because \(b-2\) divides \(b^{n}-2^{n}\) and hence any sum of numbers of the form \(b^{n}-2^{n}\) ).
